core_obligations: Identify and enumerate the relevant primes: use Ass_S(Nbar) = Ass_Sbar(Nbar), finiteness of associated primes over the Noetherian ring Sbar, and the description of zerodivisors as the union of associated primes to write Sigma = S minus (q_1 union ... union q_r) with {q_1, ..., q_r} = Ass_S(Nbar) (proof lines 1801-1808).

Transfer the description through the localisation: combine the description of Spec(Sigma^{-1}S) with the standard localisation lemma to see that the primes of Sigma^{-1}S correspond exactly to the primes q of S contained in one of the q_i (proof lines 1809-1814).

Conclude semi-locality: the maximal ideals of Sigma^{-1}S therefore correspond one-to-one with the maximal elements of {q_1, ..., q_r} with respect to inclusion, which are associated primes of Nbar over Sbar, so Sigma^{-1}S is semi-local and its spectrum consists of primes contained in an element of Ass_S(Nbar) (proof lines 1815-1817).
proof_roadmap: Rewrite the associated primes: Ass_S(Nbar) = Ass_Sbar(Nbar) because Sbar = S/m_R S, and this set is finite since Sbar is Noetherian (proof lines 1801-1806).
Rewrite the multiplicative set: Sigma coincides with the complement of the union of the associated primes because the zerodivisors on Nbar are exactly that union (proof lines 1807-1808).
Read off the primes of the localisation and identify the maximal ideals with the maximal elements of the finite set of associated primes (proof lines 1809-1817).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the spectrum of the localisation Sigma^{-1}S where Sigma is the set of elements that are not zerodivisors on the fibre module Nbar = N/m_R N: it must be shown semi-local, with primes contained in an associated prime of Nbar, and with maximal ideals in bijection with the associated primes of Nbar over Sbar (statement lines 1792-1797). The argument is a chain of identifications rather than a construction, but the identification Sigma = S minus the union of the associated primes is what makes the localisation computable, and the two hypotheses that Sbar is Noetherian and Nbar finite over Sbar are both needed to make that union finite (proof lines 1801-1814). Every step is a citation of a standard commutative-algebra lemma, so the claim is H2.
